prompts.text: Which part of an ordinary evening together do you look forward to most?
Tell me about a quiet night we spent together that you still remember fondly.
We have an unexpected evening free and nowhere we need to be. What would make it feel well spent?
An evening without a plan sometimes feels more personal than a carefully organised date.
Cooking something simple together or ordering food and choosing a film?
I like how our conversations take a different direction when neither of us is rushing.
What helps you switch from a busy day into spending relaxed time with me?
The power goes out during our evening at home. How should we make the most of it?
What is a small thing we once did at home that made the whole evening better?
When do you feel we have enough time to enjoy each other's company without checking the clock?
What is something about you that you think I understand better now than when we first met?
Tell me about a moment when I understood what you meant before you found the right words.
You're trying to explain a feeling you don't fully understand yet. What would you want me to do first?
Feeling heard matters more to me than having an immediate solution to every problem.
Talking something through while walking or sitting together somewhere quiet?
Sometimes the questions we ask each other matter more than the answers we give.
Is there a part of your personality you wish people noticed more often?
One of us comes home unusually quiet. What would be a gentle way to check in without making assumptions?
What conversation between us helped you feel more comfortable being yourself?
How do you like me to show I've understood you when we see things differently?
What's a small gesture from me that makes an ordinary day easier for you?
Tell me about a time an unexpected bit of thoughtfulness made you smile.
I know you're having a tiring week but don't want a fuss. What would be a helpful surprise?
Remembering the little details someone mentions is one of the nicest ways to show attention.
A thoughtful message in the middle of the day or a favourite snack waiting at home?
The gestures we barely think about often become the ones we remember later.
What kind of help do you appreciate most when you're focused on something important?
I notice you've forgotten to take a proper break. How would you prefer I bring it up?
What is one thoughtful thing someone did for you that you still try to do for others?
How do you tell the difference between someone giving you space and someone seeming distant?
What is the most harmless thing we regularly tease each other about?
Tell me about a time we both started laughing and couldn't easily explain why.
We have to invent a silly award for each other. What would mine be for?
A shared joke gets funnier when nobody else understands why it matters.
A ridiculous nickname that sticks or an ongoing joke from one memorable day?
I notice we sometimes find the same ordinary situations funny for completely different reasons.
Which of my expressions or reactions makes you laugh even when I don't mean to?
We have to tell a funny story about us at a gathering. Which one would you choose?
What is a time I tried to be serious but accidentally made you laugh?
What sort of humour helps you feel relaxed when we've both had a long day?
Which routine we've developed together would you miss if our schedules changed?
Tell me about a habit we started without ever formally deciding to do it.
Our usual weekend routine gets interrupted for a month. What part should we find a way to keep?
Familiar routines feel special when both people still choose to make time for them.
A regular breakfast together or a short evening walk after work?
Our small habits say a lot about how we make room for each other.
What part of our daily rhythm feels easiest for you at the moment?
We decide to try one new shared habit for two weeks. What would be worth experimenting with?
What's a routine from your childhood you'd enjoy bringing into our time together?
How do you prefer we keep in touch on days when our schedules barely overlap?
What do you enjoy doing alone that helps you feel refreshed when we meet again?
Tell me about a time having space for yourself made you more present in a relationship.
We both have a free Saturday, but one of us wants solitude. How would you like us to talk about it?
Being comfortable with separate interests makes our shared stories more interesting.
Having a quiet hour to ourselves at home or each going out to do something different?
I like when we return from separate activities with something new to tell each other.
What helps you ask for personal time without worrying the other person will misunderstand?
I want to join an activity you usually enjoy on your own. How should I ask whether you'd welcome company?
What's something you learnt about yourself while pursuing an interest independently?
Which boundaries around rest and personal space feel natural to you?
What kinds of conversations do you enjoy having with me during a walk or drive?
Tell me about a journey we took where the conversation became the best part.
We get caught in slow traffic with no urgent deadline. What would you like us to talk about?
Some of our easiest conversations happen when we're looking at the world rather than at each other.
A long walk through a familiar neighbourhood or a short drive to somewhere neither of us has visited?
I notice new surroundings sometimes bring out stories we haven't told each other before.
Is there a place nearby where you'd enjoy going purely to talk for a while?
We're taking a train with no phone signal for an hour. How should we spend the journey?
What's a conversation we had while travelling that stayed with you afterwards?
What makes a shared journey feel relaxing to you, even when the destination isn't special?
What's one preference of mine you've grown to appreciate even though it isn't naturally yours?
Tell me about a time we found a solution neither of us had thought of at first.
We want different things for dinner and neither option matters much. How should we choose?
Compromise feels easier when we treat the decision as something we're solving together.
Taking turns choosing weekend activities or finding something new we both want to try?
Our differences sometimes help us notice options we'd otherwise overlook.
Which small decisions do you prefer making together, and which do you enjoy leaving to one person?
We have two good ideas for a day out but only enough time for one. What would make the decision fair?
What is a harmless disagreement between us that became funny in hindsight?
How do you like us to revisit a decision when one of us changes their mind?
What is one detail from our early conversations that still makes you smile?
Tell me about a day together that felt ordinary at the time but means more to you now.
We make a small memory box of our time together. What everyday item would you put inside?
Our favourite memories don't always come from the occasions we spent the most money on.
Looking through old photographs together or replaying songs we listened to when we first met?
I sometimes remember the smallest details of our first few outings more clearly than the big plans.
What's something about our relationship you didn't expect when we were first getting to know each other?
We have to choose one photo to represent a recent month together. What moment would it show?
What is a kind thing we said to each other early on that you still remember?
How has your idea of a comfortable day together changed since we became closer?
What's a simple experience you'd enjoy sharing with me sometime this year?
Tell me about a plan you once made with someone that turned out better because it stayed flexible.
We have a modest budget for a free weekend. What would you prioritise: food, activities or time to rest?
Having something small to look forward to together is sometimes enough to brighten a busy week.
Planning a short day trip or setting aside a whole day with no fixed schedule?
Our plans feel more enjoyable when there's room for one of us to suggest something unexpected.
What new place would you like us to visit for no reason other than spending time together?
We each choose one activity for a shared weekend. How would you like us to combine them?
What's a plan we postponed that you still think would be worth revisiting?
What would make the next few months feel balanced between trying new things and enjoying familiar routines?
